newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper editorials - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper editorials - June 23.

text.p: There are eight days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said China's People's Liberation Army used to be a clean army, but in recent years many army officers were involved in business dealings and abused their power and priviledges. The paper said that because of the Tiananmen massacre, Hong Kong people were scared of the PLA, so it would be better for the garrison to enter the territory in a low key fashion. From a long-term point of view, the PLA should consider recruiting locally to improve its relationship with Hong Kong people, it said.

-- SING TAO said it was encouraging that leaders of the Group of Seven nations expressed confidence that China will kepp its promises on Hong Kong, adding that those who are suspicious should not do anything harmful during this sensitive period. What was important now was not to argue over past issues but to look forward and try to ensure that the present good system of Hong Kong would develop in the right direction. The paper said that after the handover, international attention will be good for Hong Kong's economic development.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said the task of the provisional legislature before the handover had been completed. As the first legislature reflecting "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong", the paper said the council had established a new legislative culture -- most of its members had a high sense of responsibility over carrying out the "one country, two systems" policy and conducted their jobs seriously and positively. History will record the contributions of the provisional legislature to Hong Kong's peaceful handover, it said.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said that on his first visit to Hong Kong, PLA Major-General Liu Zhenwu said that the media was a "very important bridge" between the PLA and the public. But unless he appointed a press spokesman, who could swiftly respond to unfavourable stories, then that bridge could not operate, and further public relations disasters were inevitable, the paper said.
